B4.v: Integrated workbook for selecting the best printing cylinder/repeat, calculating web consumption, estimating machine cost, depreciation, and job selling price.

B5.v: 1) Enter job dimensions and quantity in JOB_INPUTS. 2) Review compatible cylinder options in CYLINDER_SELECTOR. 3) Confirm production assumptions. 4) Enter machine and cost parameters in MACHINE_COST. 5) Review total cost and selling price in JOB_COSTING.

B8.v: Candidate repeat = cylinder teeth × 3.175 mm. The system calculates labels-around, actual gap, repeat utilization and ranks compatible cylinders.

B9.v: The current source file mixes manual inputs, formulas and pricing assumptions in one sheet. This rebuild separates master data, engineering calculations and costing to reduce errors.

B4.v: The original workbook combines job data, cylinder selection, material consumption and pricing assumptions on one REVISION sheet.

B5.v: Cylinder selection is partly manual: a list of available tooth counts is tested against label length and a fixed minimum gap formula.

B6.v: The source uses 3.175 mm per cylinder tooth, which is retained in the new selector.

B7.v: Material width logic and repeat logic are separated from costing in the new system so changes to label dimensions update downstream calculations.

B8.v: Original pricing formulas use assumptions such as 50 m setup allowance per color, 2,000 m roll length and a profit/markup calculation. These are now editable inputs.

B9.v: Machine depreciation was not structurally separated. The new workbook calculates hourly depreciation for the flexo press, inspection machine and slitting/rewinding machine independently.

B10.v: All zero-cost values in MACHINE_COST are intentionally editable because machine purchase values, energy tariff and labor costs must come from your actual factory figures.

B11.v: Recommendation: validate the final selected cylinder against the actual press gear standard, plate thickness, mounting tape and OEM repeat chart before production.
